submitted.body:
The paper gives an explicit rank-four binary matroid on E = {0,...,8}, with x = 1 and y = 6. Each deletion admits a partition into two bases, yet no pair of such partitions shares a base. The construction uses parallel elements, which the printed conjecture permits. It refutes the conjecture in that full scope; no simple-matroid counterexample, minimality, infinite family, or refutation of White's conjecture is claimed.

**Result and scope:** An actual rank4 matroid on9 labeled elements, with k2 and x1,y6, has two-base partitions of both deletions but no choices of such partitions share a base. Parallel elements permitted by source; full literal conjecture negation.

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [A rank-four nine-element counterexample to Lason common-basis conjecture](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00061) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00061v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.
